This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland will challenge Chuck Schumer to lead senate Democrats.
Both men have decades of experience on Capitol Hill.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has more.
Schumer's been in elected office in Washington for 45 years, Van Hollen for about 25.
But the Maryland Democrat, who's run Democrats' campaign efforts in both chambers
and is a former deputy to Speaker Nancy Pelosi, is positioning himself as a change candidate.
He's got some high-profile backers in his corner, including Abdul Elsayed of Michigan and Bernie Sanders of Vermont.
But he'll need nearly 30 Democrats in a secret ballot vote to get across the finish line.
For now, leader Schumer is projecting confidence.
He's led Democrats for a decade and said he has the support necessary to secure re-election as leader.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump departs for a run of high-level symmetry in Asia.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports that this includes an unprecedented three-way meeting Thursday with the leaders of Russia and China.
Trump's first stop is Manila, the Philippines, where he will attend a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN.
From there, it's on to the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Organization summit.
Trump has said he wants to negotiate a new arms control deal with Russia and China.
But China, which has the smallest nuclear arsenal of the three, is not likely to be interested.
Trump will also try to extend a truce in the U.S.'s trade war with China.
Trump's critics are concerned that Trump could side with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping
in deciding the fate of smaller actors such as Ukraine and Taiwan without their participation or consent.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
Iranian forces say they launched a retaliatory attack on U.S. radar systems at an air base in Bahrain overnight.
It's the second such attack since Friday.
NPR's Aya Batrani reports from Dubai.
Iran's state media reported the sound of explosions in Iranian territory near the Strait of Hormuz after midnight Sunday without elaborating further.
Soon after, Iran's Revolutionary Guard issued a statement saying it had delivered a "crushing response" to U.S. military aggression
by launching six drones targeting a U.S. radar in Bahrain.
It said it launched this number of drones to ensure the U.S. understands any act of aggression will be met with a severe response.
Bahrain confirmed the Iranian attack, saying its air defenses intercepted them all.
U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to NPR's request for comment.
The apparent tit-for-tat attacks come as Iran continues attacking oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, including it says two on Sunday with mines.
Aya Batrani, NPR News, Dubai.
Japan's economy unexpectedly contracted in the third quarter at a 0.1 rate, slowing because of higher energy prices, according to figures released on Monday.
Economists had expected the economy to grow.
It's NPR.
This weekend, City Field, which is the home of the New York Mets, hosted the sixth annual New York Bagel Fest,
a celebration of the round-baked Jewish delicacy most often served with lox and cream cheese.
Thousands attended, including reporter Jeff London.
Who doesn't love a doughy, chewy bagel?
Over 50 vendors from New York City across the United States and even abroad attended this year's event,
handing out samples from their kitchens to an appreciative crowd which voted for their favorite bagels.
Professionals did, too, and at the end of the day, a winner was crowned.
The 2026 New York Bagel Fest Best Bagel Award goes to Essa Bagel Award!
The local company with several outlets in Manhattan and Brooklyn is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year,
and the win was the Schmear on the top of the bagel.
For NPR News, I'm Jeff London in New York.
Both the NTSB and FAA are investigating Saturday night's ground collision at Miami International Airport,
this between a Boeing 767 from UPS, which had just landed,
and a Copa Airline 737, which was taxing to a runway for takeoff.
Two people suffered minor injuries when a wingtip on the Copa jet struck the nose of the UPS plane,
which caused significant damage to the aircraft.
Copa Airline said in a statement it regrets the disruption the incident may have caused our passengers.
Two months ago, a collision at Miami Airport killed five.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News.
